GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI,
DEPARTMENT OF WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT & GANGA REJUVENATION
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. †4213
ANSWERED ON 18.07.2019
WATER RESOURCES REVIVAL SCHEME
†4213. SHRI JANARDAN MISHRA
SHRI RODMAL NAGAR
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government has formulated a scheme to revive river system like rivulets etc. by carrying
out rain water harvesting;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) if not, the steps being taken by the Government for conservation of such river systems; and
(d) the steps taken by the Government for conservation of water of Kanthi river in Guna district of
Madhya Pradesh?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI & SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT
(SHRI RATTAN LAL KATARIA)
(a) to (d) There is no specific scheme to revive the river system by carrying out rain water harvesting.
However, the Government of India has taken a number of initiatives for river rejuvenation. The work of
development of River Ganga and its tributaries is undertake n by Ministry of Jal Shakti under National
Mission for Clean Ganga. The development work for rest of the rivers is undertaken under the National
River Conservation Plan. A number of State s have also taken up rejuvenation of small rivers under
schemes like MGNREGA
A National Perspective Plan for Water Resources Development has been formulated by MoWR,
RD & GR for transfer of water from surplus river basins to water deficit river basins.
Hon’ble NGT vide order dated 20.09.2018 in OA No 673/2018 has directed State Governments
and UT Administrations for preparation of action plans and its execution within 2 years (from 1 st April,
2019) for bringing all the polluted river stretches to be fit at least for bathing purposes. The action plans to
be prepared by River Rejuvenation Committee of concerned State includes various aspects such as source
control (municipal sewage management, industrial pollution control, waste management), river
catchment/basin management (adoption of good irrigation practices, utilization of treated sewage, ground
water recharge aspects), flood plain zone protection and its management (setting up of bio -diversity parks,
removal of encroachments, plantation on both sides of the river), environmental flow, watershed
management and rain water harvesting.
Water being a State subject, steps for augmentation, conservation and efficient management of
water resources are undertaken by the respective State Governments. In order to supplement the efforts of
State Governments, Ministry of Jal Shakti provides technical and financial assistance to State
Governments through various schemes. U nder the National River Conservation Plan, project proposals
received from the State Government a re considered for financial assistance on cost sharing basis between
the Central and State Government. As intimated by the Government of Madhya Pradesh, at present, there
is no proposal for conservation of Kanthi river.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 4214 
ANSWERED ON 18TH JULY, 2019 
 
LAND ACQUISITION FOR ROAD PROJECTS 
 
4214.  SHRI AJAY MISRA TENI: 
 
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
सडक परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government is aware that the issue of land acquisition has been the biggest 
reason for pendency of road projects during the period from 2004 to 2014 across the country;  
(b)  if so, the details thereof;  
(c)  whether there was no proper and beneficial policy regarding land acquisition in the 
interest of the people; and  
(d)  if so, the remedial measures taken/ being taken by the Government after the year 2014 to 
remove the shortcomings in the said policy and expedite the road projects? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
 
 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
 
(a) and (b)  National Highway projects are delayed due to various reasons viz. utility shifting, 
non-availability of soil/ aggregate, poor performance of contractors, environment/ forest/ wildlife 
clearances, Road Over Bridge (ROB) & Road Under Bridge (RUB)  issues with Railways, public 
agitation for additional facilities, arbitration/ contractual disputes with contractors including 
hurdles in land acquisition.  
 
(c) The land for the building, maintenance, management or operation of a national highway 
or part thereof, is acquired under the National Highways (NH) Act, 1956 . The NH Act, 1956 
was amended vide Act No. 16 of 1997 whereby the provisions for acquisition of land for the 
National Highways were made under Section 3 of the NH Act, 1956.  
 
(d) The Ministry of Road Transport & Highways has taken following  remedial measures to 
expedite the land acquisition for road projects: 

i. Determination of compensation for land acquisition for NHs in consonance with 
the applicable provisions of t he Right to Fair Compensation and Tra nsparency 
in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement  (RFCTLARR) Act, 2013, 
w.e.f. 01.01.2015. T he stipulations contained in the RFCTLARR Act, 2013 
prescribes for:  
(i)  The higher value amongst prevailing circle -rates or average of highest 
50% of sales -transactions of past 03 years shall be the market value of 
land;  
(ii)  Value of land in rural areas is multiplied by a factor determined by the 
‘appropriate’ Government; and,  
(iii)  Solatium @100% is payable on the sum of: (a) market value of land 
(multiplied by factor) and, (b) value of assets thereon (i.e. crops, trees, 
ponds, buildings, bore-wells, structures etc.);  
(iv)  Interest @ 12% per annum is paid on marke t value of land from date of 
3A/ 3D Notification till the date of taking possession or payment of 
compensation, whichever is earlier.  
ii. Completion of major portion of land acquisition prior to initiation of bid; 
iii. Constitution of High Power Committee under Chief Secretary to resolve the 
issue related to land acquisition; 
iv. Delegation of powers to Regional Officers for speedier decision making; 
v. Engagement of retired revenue personnel at Regional Officer/ Project Director 
level as well as at Competent Authority for La nd Acquisition level to assist in 
Land Acquisition matters; 
vi. Introduction of BhoomiRashi portal for online submission of Land Acquisition 
notification for reducing the time in publication; 
vii. Regular review at the level of Hon’ble Minister for Road Transport &  
Highways, Secretary, Ministry of Road Transport & Highways and Chairman, 
National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) and other senior officers; 
viii. Close coordination with other Ministries and State Governments;

Piped Drinking Water Supply 
 
4215. SHRI ANUBHAV MOHANTY: 
 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether only 18 per cent of the rural househol ds are getting piped drinking water 
supply and if so, the facts thereof; 
 (b)  whether the Union Government is planning to c ome up with schemes in 
coordination with the respective State Governments to provide piped drinking 
water to every household in the rural areas by 2024; and 
 (c)  if so, the manner in which the Union Governme nt proposes to coordinate with the 
State Government of Odisha and the time by which it plans to start the scheme?  
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FORJAL SHAKTI 
(SHRI RATTAN LAL KATARIA) 
 
(a)  As reported by States on Integrated Management  Information System (IMIS), out 
of total 17.87 crore rural households in the countr y, about 3.27 crore (i.e. 18.33%) rural 
household are getting drinking water from tap connection. 
 
(b) & (c) As announced in the Union Budget Speech 2 019-20, it has been envisaged to 
ensure piped water supply to all rural households b y 2024 under the Jal Jeevan Mission. 
This Programme, under the Department of Drinking Wa ter and Sanitation, will focus on 
integrated demand and supply side management of wat er at the local level, including 
creation of local infrastructure for source sustain ability like rainwater harvesting, 
groundwater recharge and management of household wastewater for reuse in agriculture. 
The Jal Jeevan Mission will converge with other Central and State Government Schemes 
including those in the State of Odisha to achieve i ts objectives of sustainable water 
supply management across the country.

:

implementing the following programmes and schemes for promotion and to modernize Khadi
 
and Village Industries in the country, including the State of Tamil Nadu:

Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP)
 
is a credit linked subsidy 
scheme, for setting up of new micro
-
enterprises and to generate employment opportunities in 
r
ural as well as urban areas of the country through KVIC, State Khadi & Village Industries

g sector and Rs.10 lakh in the service sector.

: 2 :

Rural Engineering and Bio
-
Technology Industry (REBT)

Service & Te
xtile Industry

weavers, increased artisans’ welfare and to achieve synergy with 
village industries.

Khadi

Empowerment, (ii) Direct Reform Assistance to 400 Khadi Institutions & (iii) 
Implementation of a well
-
knit MIS.

Scheme of Fund for Rege
neration of Traditional Industries (SFURTI)
 
has been under 
implementation since 2005
-
06 for making Traditional Industries more productive and 
competitive by organizing the Traditional Industries and artisans into clusters. The Scheme 
envisages providing ne
ed
-
based assistance for replacement of production equipment, setting

SFURTI scheme d
uring 2016

17.

-
departmental training centres. These training centres imparts need

based training

ems, Bakery Products,

cturing techniques of the

arch & Development schemes of

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 4217 
ANSWERED ON 18TH  JULY, 2019 
 
CONSTRUCTION OF BYPASS ON NH-15 
4217.   SHRI DILIP SAIKIA: 
             Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
                        सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether 30 to 37 km stretch (Senglipara to Lengripara) under National Highway No. 15 
is passing through congested city and causing several road accidents regularly;  
(b) if so, the details thereof along with the reaction of the Government thereto; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to construct bypass on the said NH and if so, the 
details thereof; 
(d) whether the Government has prepared DPR in this regard and if so, the details thereof; 
and  
(e) the time by which construction of said bypass is likely to be completed? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
 
(a) to (e)  The existing road from km. 30 to km. 37 (Senglipara to Lengripara ) on NH -15 
passing through Mangaldoi Town is facing traffic congestion due to growth in traffic volume. To 
avoid traffic congestion, consultancy service for preparation of DPR for construction of bypass 
(Mangaldoi Bypass) from km 30.00 to km 42.00 of NH -15 (Old NH 52) is taken up. Alignment 
of bypass has already been approved in -principle by Ministry subject to vetting of Local 
Administration and Town & Country Planning Department. Construction depends on State 
Government vetting of alignment, acquisition of land and availability of funds.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 4219 
ANSWERED ON 18TH JULY, 2019 
 
WIDENING OF NATIONAL HIGHWAYS 
 
4219. SHRI SHANMUGA SUNDARAM K.: 
 
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
सडक़ परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) started the project of 
widening of National Highway from Chengapalli to Neelambur and from Madukkarai to 
Walayar in 2010 under Built Operate Transfer Mode  with an estimated cost of Rs. 850 
crore and if so, the details and the present status thereof;  
 
(b)  the expected time to complete the work on stretch of Madukkarai-Walayar and the steps 
 taken by the Government to expedite the work on the said project;  
 
(c)  the estimated cost and time to widen the Chengapalli to Neelambur stretch into six -lane 
 and the Madukkarai to Walayar stretch into four-lane;  
 
(d)  whether NHAI is facing cost escalation and delay in funding the said projects; and  
 
(e)  if so, the details thereof and the remedial steps taken to complete the projects at the 
 earliest? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
 
 (a) to (c) The project of 6-laning from Chengapalli to start of Coimbatore Bypass  (Neelambur) 
and 4-laning from Madukkarai to Walayar was awarded on DBFOT (Toll) basis with 
an estimated cost of Rs.852.00 crore . The work on this road stretch started in 
September, 2010 with scheduled completion period of 30 months. The project was 
delayed due to land acquisition and financial constraint faced by the Concessionaire. 
The Provisional Commercial Operation Date (PCOD) for Chengapalli - Neelambur 
stretch was issued on 09.10.2015, whereas four lane work on main carriageway and 
service road on the stretch of Madukkarai-Walayar was completed on 31.07.2017. 
 As regards construction of side d rain in RE wall portion  in Madukkarai-Walayar 
stretch, the Concessionaire had requested for Change of Scope which was not accepted 
as the same was under original scope of work as per the Concession Agreement. After 
various review meetings, the work for construction of drain in RE wall portion and 
toilet in Truck lay bye portion has been started by Concessionaire. 
(d) & (e) As this is a DBFOT (Toll) project, the issue of cost escalation and delay in funding 
does not arise.

MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI,

PRIVATE SECTOR PARTICIPATION IN WATER RESOURCES MANAGEMENT
4220. SHRI KRIPANATH MALLAH
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government is considering to encourage private sector participation in planning,
development and management of water resources projects in the country;
(b) if so, whether any feasibility study has been conducted by the Government regarding the costs of such
efforts; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI & SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT
(SHRI RATTAN LAL KATARIA)
(a) to (c) Water being a State subject, planning, development and management of water resources projects
are done by the State Governments . State Governments do involve private companies for preparation of
project reports, execution of the projects, etc., depen ding on the need. Further, the National Water Policy
2012 inter alia stipulates that water resources projects and services should be managed with community
participation.  For improved delivery on sustainable basis, the State Governments/Urban Local Bodie s
may associate private sector in public private partnership mode

4221. SHRI SRIRANGA APPA BARNE 
          DR. SHRIKANT EKNATH SHINDE 
 
Will the Minister of NEW AND RENEWABLE ENERGY be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether integration of renewables, including hydro, is unlikely to be a concern in the next 
three to five years, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether renewable energy is faced with the problems such as piling up of payments’ 
policy hurdles and regulatory concerns in some cases;  
(c) if so, the details thereof along with the reasons therefor; 
(d) whether renegotiation of power purchases agreement s (PPAs) has not resulted in 
reduction of tariffs; 
(e) if so, the details thereof along with the reasons therefor; and 
(f) the steps taken by the Government to address the problems faced by the renewable energy 
sector? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (I/C) FOR NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY AND POWER 
AND MINISTER OF STATE FOR SKILL DEVELOPMENT & ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
(SHRI R. K. SINGH) 
 
(a) Yes Sir.  In order to integrate increasing share of renewable energy into the grid, a 
number of policy and regulatory measures have been undertaken. These include flexible 
operation of conventional generation projects, forecasting and scheduling of renewable 
power, setting up of Green Energy Corridors, and establishing Renewable Energy 
Management Centres. 
 
(b) and (c) Delay in payment by some Distribution Companies to renewable energy 
producers and delay in adoption of the tariff arrived at through competitive biddin g process 
by some of the State Electricity Regulatory Commissions are  some of the problems faced by 
the renewable energy sector. 
 
(d) and (e) In the year 2017, in Uttar Pradesh, negotiation of Power Purchase Agreements 
(PPAs) for renewable energy projects undertaken as per direction of Uttar Pradesh Electricity 
Regulatory Commission (UPERC) led to reduction in tariff. This was done since the rates 
obtained through competitive bidding process appeared to the UPERC on much higher side.  
No other instance has  been reported to the Government of India, where negotiation of PPAs 
between buyers and sellers of electricity from renewable energy projects has led to reduction 
in tariff. 
 
(f) In addition to the s teps mentioned in reply to part a)  above, other measures  taken to 
address the problems faced by the renewable energy sector include: a) guidelines for 
transparent tariff based bidding for solar and wind power projects; b) creation of Payment 
Security Mechanism; c) waiver of Inter -State Transmission Charges and l osses; and d) 
notification of standards for deployment of solar photovoltaic system/devices.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI,
DEPARTMENT OF WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT & GANGA REJUVENATION
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 4224
ANSWERED ON 18.07.2019
RIVER INTER-LINKING
4224. PROF. SAUGATA RAY
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state:
(a) the present status of river inter-linking in the country;
(b) the expected tenure of the completion of the ongoing linking projects;
(c) whether the river inter -linking will help to face drought and flood in the country, if so, the details
thereof;
(d) whether any State opposed to the project; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI & SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT
(SHRI RATTAN LAL KATARIA)
(a) The National Perspective Plan (NPP) was prepared by the then Ministry of Irrigation (now Ministry of
Jal Shakti) in August 1980 for water resources development through inter basin transfer of water, for
transferring water from water surplus basins to water -deficit basins. Under the NPP, the National Water
Development Agency (NWDA) has identified 30 links (16 under Peninsular Component and 14 under
Himalayan Component) for preparation of Feasibility Reports (FRs). The details of above river linking
projects viz., rivers, States concerned are given at Annexure-I.
Under the NPP, four priority links have also been identified for preparation of Detailed Project
Reports (DPRs) under the Peninsular Rivers Component viz; Ken -Betwa link project (KBLP),
Damanganga-Pinjal link project, Par -Tapi-Narmada link project and Godavari -Cauvery link project.
Based on the concurrence of the concerned States, DPRs of KBLP, Damanganga -Pinjal link project and
Par-Tapi-Narmada link project have been completed and sent to concerned States.
Various statutory clearances except Stage-II forest clearance & clearance from Central Empowered
Committee (CEC) of Hon’ble Supreme Court have been accorded for components under KBLP Phase -I.
The clearances for the projects proposed under KBLP Phase-II are in advanced stages. The comprehensive
DPR of the KBLP has been completed and circulated to Governments of Uttar Pradesh (UP) and Madhya
Pradesh (MP). Draft Memorandum of Agreement for implementation of KBLP has been sent to
Governments of MP and UP for concurrence.
Contd…P/2

//2//
The techno -economic clearance to the Damanganga -Pinjal link project has also been accorded
subject to statutory clearances. The DPR of Par -Tapi-Narmada has been sent to Central Water
Commission for appraisal . Draft Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for implementation of
Damanaganga-Pinjal and Par -Tapi-Narmada link projects has also been sent to Governments of
Maharashtra and Gujarat for concurrence.
The Draft DPR of Godavari -Cauvery link project consisting of three projects viz; Godavari
(Inchampalli/Janampet)-Krishna(Nagarjunasagar), Krishna (Nagarjunasagar) - Pennar(Somasila),
Pennar(Somasila)-Cauvery(Grand Anicut) link projects has been completed and circulated to party States.
(b) The stage of implementation of a project would be reached after its DPR is prepared with the
consensus of concerned States and the requisite statutory clearances are obtained. The estimated time for
implementation will depend upon the construction schedule as per DPR.
(c) The interlinking of rivers (ILR) project envisages diversion of waters from surplus basins to deficit
basins through inter basin water transfer links. The interlinking of rivers project will provide benefits to
irrigation, domestic and industrial needs, hydropower apart from the incidental benefits of flood control,
drought mitigation, navigation, water supply, fisheries, salinity and pollution control etc.
(d) & (e) Some of the States have certain views/observations regarding ILR Projects and the link -wise
details of views/observations raised by these State Governments are given at Annexure-II.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

DEPARTMENT OF WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT & GANGA REJUVENATION
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 4226
ANSWERED ON 18.07.2019
INCLUSION OF RIVER BANK EROSION UNDER NATIONAL CALAMITY
4226. SHRI PRADYUT BORDOLOI
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Union Government is aware that the State of Assam has been demanding for since ten
years that river bank erosion along with recurring floods be included in the definition of National
Calamity; and
(b) if so, the details thereof and the reaction of the Union Government thereto?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI & SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT
(SHRI RATTAN LAL KATARIA)
(a) & (b) The recurrent flood problem in Assam leads to loss of life, property and creates ecological
imbalance. Flood is a natural calamity and is attributed to various factors like wide variation in rainfall,
both in time and space with frequent departure from normal pattern, inadequate carrying capacities of
rivers, river bank erosion, silting of river beds, landslides, poor natural drainage, snow melts and glacial
lake out bursts. Under the existing Scheme of State Disaster Response Fund/National Disaster Response
Fund of Ministry of Home Affairs, there is no such provision to declare any disaster including flood as a
“National Problem/Calamity”. However, in the event of disaster of a ‘severe nature’, financial assistance
towards the notified natural disasters includi ng flood is met from the State Disaster Response Fund
(SDRF) which is further supplemented from the cess -based fund of National Disaster Response Fund
(NDRF) in accordance with the established procedure, which includes an assessment based on the visit of
an Inter-Ministerial Central Team

WATER STORAGE SCHEME UNDER PMKSY
4227. DR. FAROOQ ABDULLAH
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state:
(a) whether Arzan Garzan water storage scheme at Chrawani was approved in the year 2014 under
PMKSY and if so, the details thereof;
(b) whether the work on the said scheme was stopped after a few month; and
(c) if so, the details thereof along with the reasons therefor?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI & SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT
(SHRI RATTAN LAL KATARIA)
(a) A cluster of 117 Surface Minor Irrigation (SMI) schemes including Arzan Garzan water storage
scheme was included under Accelerated Irrigation Benefits Programme (AIBP) during 2013 -14 with an
estimated cost of Rs.584.64 crore and target potential of 41852 hectare. Total Central Assistance (CA) of
Rs.80.326 crore has been releas ed for these schemes up to March, 2019. Irrigation potential of 19659 ha
has been created up to March, 2019. The estimated cost of Arzan Garzan scheme is Rs.25.2812 crore with
planned potential creation (CCA) of 1022 hectare.
(b) & (c) The State Government has reported that the earth work excavation for the main dam body was
started in 2016. However, the construction work was stopped due to delay in obtaining approval of design
of the project by the constructing agency from the State Author ities.  The design has been approved now
and scheme is targeted for completion during 2020-21.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI,
DEPARTMENT OF WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT & GANGA REJUVENATION
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. †4235
ANSWERED ON 18.07.2019
MAINTENANCE OF RIVER GANGA’S BANK
†4235. SHRI MUKESH RAJPUT
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government has any plan to construct STP at Farrukhabad to make the bank of River
Ganga clean;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the time by which it will be completed;
(c) whether the Government proposes to have electric crematorium at the cremation sites on the banks of
River Ganga; and
(d) if so, the details thereof including Farrukhabad?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI & SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT
(SHRI RATTAN LAL KATARIA)
(a)  A project “Interception, Diversion & Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs) works and 15 years operation
& maintenance” at Farrukhabad -Fatehgarh at an estimated cost of Rs.213.62 crores has been sanctioned
under Namami Gange Programme with 100% central funding.
(b) The project envisages interception of 3 drains namely  Pakkapul Drain, Tokaghat Drain and Bhairo
Ghat Drain and diverting them to 2 nos. of STPs of 28 Million Litres per Day (MLD) and 5 MLD capacity
apart from treatment of Bargadiya d rain waste water through development of constructed wetlands. The
project has been tendered with a completion period of 21 months after award of works.
(c) Ministry of Jal Shakti through National Mission for Clean Ganga (NMCG) has already sanctioned
three electric crematoria at Garulia, Naihati and Bhatpara in West Bengal along Ganga which are under
advance stage of completion.
(d) As of now there is no electric crematorium proposed in Farrukhabad.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF MINORITY AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 4237 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 18.07.2019 
 
Implementation of Sachar Committee Recommendation 
4237.  SHRI MOHAMMAD AZAM KHAN 
 
Will the Minister of MINORITY AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has formulated any policy or plan to implement the 
recommendations of Sachar Committee during the period of 2014 to 2019; 
(b) if so, the details thereof, State/district-wise; and 
(c) if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
A N S W E R 
 
MINISTER OF MINORITYAFFAIRS 
(SHRI MUKHTAR ABBAS NAQVI) 
 
(a) to (c): The Sachar Committee Report on the condition of Muslim community of India 
was submitted on 17.11.2006. The details of the status of implementation of the 
recommendations of the Sachar Committe e report are available on the website of this 
Ministry www.minorityaffairs.gov.in. During the period 2014 to 2019, the Government took 
various initiatives for the socio-economic and educational empowerment and upliftment of 
every section of the society including the six centrally notified minorities namely Jain, 
Buddhist, Sikh, Parsi, Muslim and Christian. The budget of the Ministry has increased 
from Rs 3511 crores in 2013-14 to Rs 4700 crores in 2019-20. 
The government during the last five years has provided 3.18 crores scholarships to 
students from amongst the six centrally notified Minorities namely, Jain, Buddhist, Sikh, 
Parsi, Muslim and Christian. Out of these, girls constitute more than 50% of the 
beneficiaries. The three scholarship schemes are now being implemented through the 
National Scholarship Portal and since 2015, the scholarships schemes are being 
implemented under direct benefit transfer (DBT) mode to improve the efficiency and 
bring transparency by removing duplicity and stopping pilferages. 
 
Under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram (PMJVK), during the last five years, the  
Ministry  has  sanctioned  a  number  of  projects under  the  scheme  which  includes  25  
Degree  Colleges,  1152  School  Buildings, 20228 Additional Class Rooms, 506 Hostels, 
71 ITIs, 5 Polytechnics, 411 Sadbhav  Mandaps, 92  Residential  Schools,  530  Market  
Sheds,  5090  A anganwadi  Centres, 821 Health Projects, 2285 Water Supply Projects, 
11676 Pucca Houses, etc. The State - wise   details   of   the   projects   are   available   
on   the   Ministry’s   website   at http://www.minorityaffairs.gov.in. 
 
 

 
 
During the last five years 3,93,711 youths have been provided employment oriented skill 
development training under various schemes of this ministry. 
 
During the last five years , 59,988 students have been provided free coaching under 
various coaching schemes of the ministry. 
 
The National Minorities Development and Finance Corporation (NMDFC) has provided  
concessional loans of Rs 2582.30 crores in the last five years to 5,67,794 beneficiaries 
belonging to the six centrally notified minorities for sel f-employment and income 
generating ventures.  
 
The d etails of the schemes implemented for the socio -economic and educational 
empowerment of six centrally notified minorities by Ministry of Minority Affairs  including 
the period 2014 to 2019 are as under:- 
 
Scholarships: -Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme – For Class I to X. 
-Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme – For Class XI to Ph.D. 
-Merit-cum-Means based Scholarship Scheme – For Professional and Technical 
Courses. 
-Maulana Azad National Fellowship – For M.Phil. and Ph.D 
Free Coaching and Allied Scheme (NayaSavera)  – For Competitive Examination of 
Professional Courses and Government Jobs.  
“PadhoPardesh”– Scheme of Interest Subsidy on Educational Loans for Overseas 
Studies. 
NaiUdaan - Support for students clearing P relims conducted by UPSC, State Public 
Service Commission, etc. 
HamariDharohar - A scheme to preser ve rich heritage of Indian minority communities 
under the overall concept of Indian Culture. 
JiyoParsi – Scheme for containing population decline of small minority community. 
NaiRoshni–Leadership Development of Minority Women and to instil confidence. 
Employment-orientedSkill Development Initiatives –SeekhoAurKamao 
NaiManzil – A scheme for formal school education & skilling of school dropouts. 
USTTAD (Upgrading the Skills and Training in Traditional Arts/Crafts for Development) 
and organizing of HunarHaats for providing opportunity and market support to the 
artisans and craftsmen. 
PradhanMantri Jan VikasKaryakram(PMJVK) :- It is an area development scheme. The 
Ministry h as identified 1300 backward Mino rity Concentration Areas (MCAs) for the 
implementation of this scheme. 
Maulana Azad Education Foundation (MAEF)  implements educational and employment 
related schemes:- 
-Begum Hazrat  Mahal National Scholarship for Meritorious Girls belonging to the six 
centrally notified Minorities. 
-Gharib Nawaz Employment Traini ng for providing short -term job -oriented skill 
development courses to youths belonging to minority communities. 
-Bridge Course for madarsa students & school dropouts by Aligarh Muslim University, 
Aligarh and Jamia Millia Islamia, New Delhi under Nai Manzil scheme.  

-Swachh Vidyalaya Intiative. 
NMDFCprovides concessional loansfor self -employment and income generating 
venturesto persons from the six centrally notified minorities.  
 
Further, the Prime Minister’s New 15 Point Programme for the Welfare of Minorities , is 
an overarching programme, covering various schemes/initiatives of the participating 
Ministries/Departments and is implemented throughout the country. All the 
schemes/initiatives included in the programme are implemented by the participating 
Ministries /Departments, either exclusively for or by earmarking of overall physical 
/financial targets for minorities. The programme aims to promote education as well as 
social welfare of minorities by ensuring equitable share in economic activities and 
employment t hrough existing and new schemes, enhanced credit support for self -
employment and recruitment to State and Central Government jobs. 
 
The details of the ongoing schemes/programmes are available on the website of this 
Ministry www.minorityaffairs.gov.in; www.maef.nic.in and www.nmdfc.org.

FINANCING OF HIGHWAY PROJECTS 
 
4238.     SHRI MAHABALI SINGH: 
             
                    Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS  
सडक़ परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the development and construction works of various highways are facing 
financial crisis due to the reluctance of nationalised banks to finance the same; 
 
(b) if so, the details thereof and the steps being taken by the Government to address the issue; 
 
(c) whether the Government proposes to establish a specific/dedicated financial institution 
for financing highway projects in the country on the lines of PFC and other inf rastructure 
financial institutions; 
 
(d)  if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(e)  if not, the other steps being taken by the Government for adequately financing such 
projects in the country? 
                                    
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
 
(a) &  (b) No Sir. H owever, Banking Sector has bee n raising various concerns. Ministry  is in 
continuous interaction with the lenders of  PPP projects to resolve the issue s. Steps being taken 
by the Ministry to address the concerns being raised by Banking Sector: 
(i)      Ministry is planning to share the information through its PMIS (Project Monitoring 
Information System). 
(ii)     Substitution cases are being expedited at NHAI. 
(iii)   The Model Concession Agreement (MCA) is under consideration for amendme nt taking  
into consideration most of the issues raised by Bankers. 
 
(c) to (e) Yes Sir. Recently a Memorandum of Understanding  has been signed between NHAI 
and National Investment & Infrastructure Fund (NIIF) for financing Highway Projects.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI,
DEPARTMENT OF WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT & GANGA REJUVENATION
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 4240
ANSWERED ON 18.07.2019
RAIN WATER HARVESTING PLANTS IN BENGALURU
4240. SHRI P.C. MOHAN
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state:
(a) whether Niti Aayog has reported that Bengaluru will run out of ground water by 2021;
(b) if so, the details thereof along with the measures taken by the Government towards combating the
challenge;
(c) the number of houses and buildings in Bengaluru which have Rain Water Harvesting Plants; and
(d) the measures taken by the Government so far to ensure efficient implementation of Rain Water
Harvesting in all houses and buildings with area of 1,200 s q. ft. and more as mandated by the Central
Ground Water Board?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI & SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT
(SHRI RATTAN LAL KATARIA)
(a) to (d) NITI Aayog in its report titled “Composite Water Management Index” published in June 2018,
has mentioned that 21 major cities including Bengaluru  are expected to run out of groundwater by 2020.
This is based on the estimates of annual ground water replenishment and its extraction. However, it does
not take into account the ground water availability in the deeper aquifers.
As per the information received from Bengaluru Water Supply and Sewerage Board, Government of
Karnataka, the number of houses installed with rain water harvesting system in Bengaluru is about 1.2
lakhs.
Further, as per information received from Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs , the Model
Building Bye Laws, 2016, has been issued for guidance of the States/UTs which has a chapter on
‘Rainwater Harvesting’.  The provisions of this chapter are applicable to all the buildings. 32 States / UTs,
including Karnataka, have adopted the rainwater harvesting provisions. The implementation of the
rainwater harvesting policy comes within the purview of the State Government/Urban Local Body / Urban
Development Authority.
Hon’ble Prime Minister has written a letter to all Sarpanchs on 08.06.2019 regarding the
importance of water conservation and rain harvesting and exhorted them to adopt all appropria te measures
to make water conservation a mass movement.
Contd…P/2

//2//
The issue of water conservation/harvesting was discussed with the concerned Ministers and
officials of the State Governments by Minister, Jal Shakti in a meeting held on 11.6.2019.
An ‘Inter Ministerial Committee’ under the Chairmanship of Secretary (WR, RD & GR) has
been constituted to take forward the subject of ‘Water Conservation Related Activities for Optimum
Utilization of Monsoon Rainfall’ which meets from time to time to discus s the issue of water
conservation. The Committee includes officers from different States/UTs. Last meeting of the Inter -
Ministerial Committee was held on 01/05/2019.
Cabinet Secretary discussed the issue of water conservation/harvesting with the Chief
Secretaries of the States through video-conference on 21.05.2019.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF MINORITY AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No.4246 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 18.07.2019 
 
 
CRITERIA FOR HAJ QUOTA 
 
4246.  SHRI RAJMOHAN UNNITHAN: 
 
Will the Minister of MINORITY AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether Haj Quota is provided to each State based on the Muslim population of that State 
and if so, the details thereof; 
(b)  whether the Government proposes to revise this criteria so that the quota is provided to 
each State based on the number of applicants and if so, the details thereof; and  
(c) whether the Government has called for or proposes to call global tender from other airline 
companies to get a good airfare package for Haj pilgrims and if so, the details thereof? 
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF MINORITY AFFAIRS 
(SHRI MUKHTAR ABBAS NAQVI) 
 
(a) The quota allocated to Haj Committee of India (HCoI) is distributed amongst the States/UTs 
on the basis of their respective Muslim population, based on the 2011 census figures  as well 
as on the basis of number of applications.  
 
(b) No, Sir. As per the  new Haj Policy for HCoI pilgrims for Haj 2018 -22, the surplus seats 
generated by underutilized quota of states are utilized for providing 500 seats to Mehram, 
2000 additional seats to state of Jammu &  Kashmir as a special measure, full quota to 
States/Union Territories receiving 500 or less Haj application forms and for the ladies going 
for Haj without Mehram. The quota still remaining  is further allocated to States/Union 
Territories in proportion of n umber of applications received. This year, in 18 states, 100% 
applicants are going for Haj pilgrimage.  
 
(c) The responsibility for making air travel arrangements for Haj Pilgrims selected by the Haj 
Committee of India is with the Ministry of Civil Aviation (M oCA). The Annual Bilateral 
Agreement between India and Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA) provides that the Saudi air 
transport companies will share equally without any exception the transportation of Hajis with 
the Indian national carriers. Further, as per the conditions laid down by civil aviation authority 
of Saudi Arabia, no contracts are allowed to be made with any third party for transportation 
of Hajis.  Accordingly, various airlines of India and Saudi Arabia participate in the bidding 
process for air travel of Haj pilgrims . For Haj 2019, three airlines namely Air India, Spicejet 
and Saudia Airlines are transporting pilgrims from 21 Embarkation Points.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
MINISTRY OF JAL SHAKTI,
DEPARTMENT OF WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT & GANGA REJUVENATION
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 4247
ANSWERED ON 18.07.2019
CLEANING OF RIVERS
4247. MS. LOCKET CHATTERJEE
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state:
(a) whether rivers’ cleaning work other than Ganga is being looked after by his Ministry;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the details of the budget allocated for other rivers; and
(d) whether th e Government has done any survey regarding the condition of other rivers and if so, the
details thereof and the plan to revive those rivers?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI & SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT
(SHRI RATTAN LAL KATARIA)
(a) & (b) As per notification dated 14 th June, 2019 by the President under the clause (3) of article 77 of
the Constitution regarding Amendment to the Government of India (Allocation Business) Rules, 1961,
conservation, development, management and abatement of pollution of rivers  and National River
Conservation Directorate (NRCD) have been transferred to the Ministry of Jal Shakti.
(c) National River Conservation Plan(NRCP) has so far covered polluted stretches of 34 rivers
(excluding Ganga and its tributaries) in 77 towns spread over 16 States in the country at a sanctioned cost
of Rs. 5870.54 crore and Central share of Rs. 2378.73 crore has been released to the State Government s
for implementation of various pollution abatement schemes.  The Budget allocati on for the current
financial year 2019-2020 for “National River Conservation Plan-other Basin” is Rs. 196 crore.
(d) Central Pollution Control Board(CPCB) in collaboration with the State Pollution Control
Boards is regularly monitoring the water quality of ri vers across the country through a network of
monitoring stations under the National Water Quality Monitoring Programme. Based on monitoring
results in terms of Bio -chemical Oxygen  Demand(BOD) levels, a key indicator of organic pollution,
CPCB identifi es t he polluted river stretches in the country.  As per the report published by CPCB in
February, 2015, 351 polluted river stretches have been identified on 323 rivers as per details at Annexure.
